record.eligibility: Members of the Baylor St. Luke's Medical Center (BSLMC) professional hospital staff or associated investigators may submit proposals. Health care professionals from other institutions are also invited if the project is a collaborative one involving St. Luke's staff, and clinical investigations must be conducted at BSLMC or its affiliated institutions. Before the committee will consider a proposal, the investigator must already hold IRB approval from a St. Luke's-accepted IRB (BRANY, Baylor, UT or CHI). Projects with clinical application that could improve care quality or safety of hospitalized patients at BSLMC receive highest priority. No career-stage, degree or track restriction is stated.
record.notes: The Roderick D. MacDonald Research Fund is a Baylor St. Luke's Medical Center endowment, administered through BCM's Office of Research IT page, that awards up to $50,000 for one year with five review deadlines annually (2026: Jan 7, Mar 9, May 7, Aug 7, Nov 9). It is open to BSLMC professional staff and associated investigators, and explicitly to clinicians from other institutions whose collaborative project involves St. Luke's staff and is conducted at BSLMC or an affiliate, so a BCM breast medical oncologist practicing at Baylor St. Luke's is a natural applicant. For the PI it is the quickest local source of seed money for a ctDNA/MRD or EHR pilot, a biomarker sub-study nested in an existing trial, or start-up costs for an investigator-initiated trial. The trap is sequencing: the committee will not consider a proposal until a St. Luke's-accepted IRB (Baylor, BRANY, UT or CHI) has already approved the protocol, so the IRB submission must precede the fund application by months, and the budget cannot carry indirects, travel, publication costs or more than $10,000 in salary. The committee gives highest priority to work with clinical application to the quality or safety of care for hospitalized BSLMC patients, so an outpatient breast biomarker project should articulate a concrete care-delivery payoff at St. Luke's. Applications are delivered on paper to the committee chair and the BSLMC Office of Research (Neurosensory Building, 3rd floor). Next step: obtain IRB approval for the pilot protocol now and target the November 9, 2026 deadline; the committee normally meets within three weeks of each deadline.

record.eligibility: The applicant of record must be a Rice University faculty member (any discipline) proposing a new collaborative research project with a faculty member at a Texas Medical Center health-related institution; Baylor College of Medicine qualifies as the partner institution. Rice ENRICH funds the Rice co-PI's $25,000 half; the TMC collaborator's institution must provide the matching $25,000, and in-kind support in lieu of cash match is explicitly allowed. No rank, degree, track or clinical-duty restriction is stated on the program page. Projects run 12 months from the date in the award letter with a mid-term report at 7 months and a final report at the end.
record.notes: The Rice and TMC Collaborator Fund is a rolling seed mechanism run by Rice's ENRICH office that pays $25,000 to a Rice faculty co-PI for a new collaborative health-related project with a TMC institution, contingent on the partner institution matching $25,000 in cash or in kind. For the PI, this is the standing low-friction route to a Rice-side partner on an EHR, ctDNA/MRD or imaging-analytics pilot, since Rice supplies the computational or engineering collaborator and ENRICH supplies that collaborator's half of the budget. The PI cannot apply directly: the Rice faculty member is the applicant of record and submits by email to ENRICH@rice.edu, so the first step is recruiting a Rice co-PI and securing a departmental or Duncan Cancer Center commitment (in-kind is acceptable) for the BCM half. The trap is treating this as $50,000 of new money; only $25,000 is external, it carries no F&A, and the project must finish in 12 months with a 7-month interim report. The page states that awards are rolling and proposals are accepted in FY27, and ENRICH's opportunities page says proposals are currently being accepted, so there is no deadline to wait for. Decisions come within three weeks of submission. Past awards have gone to Rice-BCM digital health and health equity projects at $50,000 each, which is a good precedent for the PI's real-world-data angle. The disease-specific fit is low because the fund is generic health research, so competitiveness rests on the novelty of the Rice-BCM pairing rather than on breast cancer relevance.

record.notes: The Coltman Fellowship is The Hope Foundation's two-year, $100,000 salary award that buys protected time for an early-career investigator at a SWOG member institution to develop a SWOG-associated clinical or translational project under a SWOG-active mentor, with travel to four consecutive SWOG Group Meetings paid on top. No indirect costs are paid and the budget is salary and fringe only. record.notes: The Hope Foundation's Secondary Data Analysis Program is a standing, rolling-submission mechanism that pairs a SWOG member investigator with the SWOG Statistics and Data Management Center to run a database analysis on completed SWOG trial data, alone or linked to SEER or SEER-Medicare claims. It is not a cash grant: the RFA states all associated funds are paid directly to the SWOG Statistical Center, so the PI receives analyst time and data access rather than budget. That makes it a direct match for the PI's first-priority angle of real-world and registry-linked outcomes work, and it is a low-cost route to a first-author cooperative-group paper drawing on SWOG breast trials with ER+ and HER2+ populations. The application is deliberately light (one-page cover letter, one-page analysis plan specifying outcomes, predictors and any claims codes, NIH-style biosketch, other support), and more than one distinct project may be submitted. The trap is membership: the applicant type is SWOG Member Investigators and membership is institutional, so the PI should confirm that BCM is an active SWOG member site and that the PI is registered, then engage the SWOG Breast Committee so the concept reads as aligned with the Group's portfolio, which reviewers score explicitly. A second caution is that the RFA is dated February 2022 even though it was re-uploaded in March 2026, and the number of projects per year is limited and funding-contingent, so the PI should email the program contact to confirm capacity before investing effort. Nothing in this program overlaps the held Impact Award or SEED Fund records; the SEED Fund also permits secondary data analysis but is a separate annual cash award.

record.career_cap: No PI or co-PI role on a clinical trial or NIH R-level grant within the past 10 years; must have completed fellowship/postdoc training
record.eligibility: Medical, surgical, gynecologic or radiation oncologists, or PhD-prepared researchers, who have completed fellowship or postdoc training. The applicant must not have been a principal investigator or co-principal investigator on a clinical trial or an NIH R-level grant within the past 10 years. Prior NRG Oncology experience or a commitment to future NRG involvement is required, along with institutional support for a minimum 10% FTE commitment and acceptance of a 10% indirect-cost cap. No degree, faculty-track or clinical-duty restriction is stated; the 2025 call named breast cancer research among the specific opportunities.
record.notes: A two-year, $50,000 ($25,000/yr) mentored fellowship run by NRG Oncology's NCORP research base that pairs an early-stage investigator with a senior NRG mentor to carry a health-care-access concept through NRG protocol development, with the fellow expected to serve as PI of the resulting trial. It is distinct from the held NRG Early Career Mentored Fellowship (April 30 cycle, unfunded) and from generic concept submission: this one carries money, a named funder slot (BCRF funded the 2026 breast fellow), and mandatory HCA Committee engagement, so it is the cleanest conversion of the PI's health-equity angle into cooperative-group trial leadership. The trap is the career cap: anyone who has been PI or co-PI on any clinical trial or NIH R-level grant in the past 10 years is ineligible, which an investigator-initiated-trial record could trigger; the PI should confirm standing before drafting. The 10% indirect cap and 10% FTE commitment need BCM and division sign-off, and the fellow must attend every summer and winter NRG meeting for two years. Applications are accepted yearly in the fall; the 2026-27 call closed September 19, 2025 and the 2022 call also closed September 19, so the 2027-28 call is likely imminent but was not posted on the program page or news feed as of 2026-09-10. Next step: watch the program page for the 2026 announcement PDF, line up an NRG breast-committee mentor, and prepare a one-page access-focused concept (for example ctDNA/MRD-guided surveillance access or ADC delivery in rural or safety-net populations) that also serves the PI's real-world-data angle. Prior calls routed applications to Fellowships@NRGOncology.org.

provenance.proven: Quantum Leap has sponsored I-SPY 2 continuously since 2010 across 16 US cancer centres and maintains a public publications library of DAPC-approved analyses; the platform's biomarker sub-study model is documented in the peer-reviewed I-SPY literature.

record.eligibility: Applicants must hold an MD, PhD, DO, PharmD or equivalent doctoral degree, be US citizens, nationals or permanent residents, and be employed by a domestic nonprofit or government entity. New applicants must have total qualifying educational debt equal to or exceeding 20 percent of institutional annual base salary at award (waived for renewals) and must commit to an average of at least 20 hours per week of qualified clinical research during each quarterly service period; NIH research funding is not required. Qualified research is patient-oriented research with human subjects, epidemiologic, behavioral, outcomes or health-services research, which covers EHR, ctDNA/MRD and registry work. Ineligible are those with a federal judgment lien, an unresolved health-professional service obligation, federal employment over 20 hours per week, any research support or salary from a for-profit organization, or current IRTA/CRTA awards; only one LRP application per fiscal year is allowed.
record.notes: The NIH Extramural Loan Repayment Program for Clinical Researchers (LRP-CR, L30) repays up to $50,000 per year of qualified educational debt for doctoral-level investigators who commit to at least 20 hours per week of clinical research at a domestic nonprofit or government employer. The FY2027 notice NOT-OD-26-081 (released July 13, 2026) confirms the cycle opened September 1, 2026 and closes November 19, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. EST, with awards starting between July 1 and September 30, 2027. It matters to the PI because there is no career-stage cap, NIH funding is not a prerequisite, and EHR, ctDNA/MRD and registry work fits squarely within NIH's definition of clinical research; it is disease-agnostic, so breast or ER+/HER2+ relevance carries no weight in review. The award is personal debt relief rather than research money, so it should be treated as a salary-support complement, not a project grant. The trap is the two hard gates: the PI must still carry educational debt of at least 20 percent of base salary at the time of award, and must be able to document, quarterly, a 50 percent research effort while holding clinical duties; a breast oncologist at 30 percent protected time cannot certify this. A further trap is the exclusion of anyone receiving research support or salary from a for-profit organization, which the PI should reconcile against industry consulting and industry-sponsored trial arrangements. Next step: confirm remaining debt balance and base salary, confirm protected research time is at least 50 percent, then register in the LRP portal, line up the mentor or institutional contact and the BCM business official certification, and submit before November 19, 2026.
record.evidence: NOT-OD-26-081 (release date "July 13, 2026"): application period "September 1 through November 19, 11:59 p.m. EST" establishes the open window and deadline; "$50,000 annually" and "at least two years" for new awards, "LRP renewal awards are available for one- or two-year periods" establish award size and duration; "total qualifying educational debt equal to or in excess of 20 percent of their institutional annual base salary" and "This criterion is not applicable to applicants for a renewal award" establish the debt gate; "awardees must engage in qualified research for an average of at least 20 hours per week during each quarterly service period" establishes the effort gate; "Research funding from NIH is not required to participate in the Extramural LRP" establishes no funding prerequisite; ineligibility includes "Individuals who receive any research funding support or salary from a for-profit institution or organization" and "No individual may submit more than one LRP application to the NIH in any fiscal year"; award start "no earlier than July 1 and no later than September 30 annually". NIH LRP landing page (grants.nih.gov/funding/funding-categories/lrp): applications open September 1, 2026, "due" "November 19, 2026," awards beginning July 1, 2027.

A minimum of 75% full-time professional effort (9 person-months) must be committed to the award; clinical duties may occupy the remaining 25%. PAR-27-112 is the Clinical Trial Not Allowed version, so the candidate cannot propose leading an independent clinical trial, though experience within a mentor-led trial is permitted.
record.notes: The Beeson K76 is NIA's leadership-track career development award, co-funded with AFAR and the John A. Hartford Foundation, paying up to $225,000 in direct costs per year for up to five years at 8% F&A. It is the one NIH K designed for a clinician who already runs funded projects: candidates must have prior competitively awarded PD/PI support at the faculty level plus demonstrated leadership, while still holding ESI status. For the PI, a fellowship completed in 2019-2020 should leave ESI intact through roughly 2029-2030, so the 2026 and 2027 receipt dates are both live, provided no R01-equivalent has been awarded. The genuine fit is a geriatric-oncology reframing of the computational angle, for example EHR or registry-based outcomes, ctDNA/MRD surveillance, or endocrine-therapy adherence in older women with ER+ breast cancer; NIA will not fund breast cancer science that merely happens to include older patients. The trap is effort: 75% protected time is mandatory, leaving 25% for clinic, which most breast medical oncologists cannot commit without an explicit institutional letter, and PAR-27-112 is the Clinical Trial Not Allowed version, so the investigator-initiated trial angle must sit outside the aims. The PI should confirm current funding history against the PD/PI requirement, secure an aging-focused co-mentor (BCM's Huffington Center on Aging or the DLDCCC geriatric oncology group), and check with NIA training staff whether November 12, 2026 (the NOFO date) or November 10 (the AFAR page) governs. A July 12, 2027 receipt date follows if the November cycle is too soon.

record.eligibility: Candidates must hold a health-professional doctoral degree (MD, DO, DDS, PharmD and others) and by award be a US citizen, non-citizen national, or permanent resident. Candidates should typically be at the midcareer stage (Associate Professor level or functioning at that rank) and must have an established record of independent, peer-reviewed patient-oriented research grant funding, including funding held at the time of application, which they are expected to keep holding through the award. Clinical duties are compatible; the award buys 25-50% protected time out of non-research patient care and administrative work. Critically, NCI is not a participating institute in either PA-24-187 or PA-24-188; participants are NHLBI, NIA, NIAAA, NIAID, NIAMS, NIDCD, NIDA, NIEHS, NIMH, NINR, NCCIH, plus NIMHD (PA-24-188 only), with ORWH and ODSS as co-funders.
record.notes: The Parent K24 (PA-24-188, clinical trial not allowed; PA-24-187, independent clinical trial required) is the NIH midcareer protected-time award for clinician-investigators doing patient-oriented research: 25-50% salary up to the cap plus $50,000 per year for up to five years, with standard NIH due dates of February 12, June 12 and October 12 through the NOFO expiration of 2027-05-08. It is verified real and open, and the next new-application date is 2026-10-12. The decisive fact the finder got wrong is that NCI is not a participating institute in either parent K24; the participants are NHLBI, NIA, NIAAA, NIAID, NIAMS, NIDCD, NIDA, NIEHS, NIMH, NINR, NCCIH, and (PA-24-188 only) NIMHD, so a breast-oncology K24 has no natural home and a cancer-focused application would be assigned nowhere. The only route for the PI is an NIMHD-assigned K24 built around a cancer health equity program, which is the PI's fourth-priority angle and would need to read as disparities-primary rather than ER+/HER2+ biology or ctDNA methods. Two further gates apply regardless: the candidate must hold independent, peer-reviewed patient-oriented research funding at the time of application, and candidates are typically at the Associate Professor level or functioning at that rank. The trap is treating this as a near-term NCI career award; it is neither NCI nor near-term. What to do next: revisit only if the PI accumulates independent equity-focused patient-oriented funding (e.g., an R01-scale or comparable peer-reviewed award) and is at or near associate rank, then check the NIMHD row of the K24 IC-specific table before investing effort; otherwise treat the record as informational.

record.notes: The Stephen I. Katz ESI R01 (PAR-25-322, reissue of PAR-24-075, open 2025-08-25 through 2028-08-26) is an uncapped, up-to-five-year NIH R01 reserved for Early Stage Investigators proposing a new research direction with no preliminary data; NCI is among the 24 participating ICs. It matters to the PI because the usual barrier to a first R01 for an MD-only clinician, the absence of a preliminary dataset, is inverted here: preliminary data are forbidden, and the review criteria instead ask for a sound premise and a credible justification of feasibility. A pivot into EHR/registry real-world-data methods or ctDNA/MRD analytics, or a biomarker-discovery project in HER2-heterogeneous or triple-positive disease, could be framed as a change in direction from a clinical-trials background, provided the PI has not already published in that exact area. The trap is twofold: any unpublished data in the application makes it noncompliant and withdrawn, and the one-page "New Research Direction" attachment is mandatory, so the PI must resist the reflex to show feasibility with a pilot analysis. The other gate is ESI standing, which runs ten years from the end of clinical training (fellowship 2019-2020, so roughly to 2029-2030) but is lost with any prior R01-equivalent award; the PI should confirm the ESI flag in the eRA Commons profile first. Clinical trials are not allowed under this NOFO, so the investigator-initiated-trial angle does not belong in this application. Standard cycles are late January, late May and late September for new applications; the 2026-09-28 date is too close to be realistic, so the PI should target 2027-01-26 (new) and contact the NCI program officer in the IC-specific table beforehand to confirm the project fits NCI's interest under this mechanism.

record.eligibility: Open to investigator-initiated, interventional, proof-of-concept, Phase I or Phase IIA clinical trials of an already-approved drug, biologic, cell/gene therapy or combination in a new indication for any "unsolved disease," conducted at an accredited academic or nonprofit research institution or health system anywhere in the world (start-ups, biotechs and pharma are not eligible). record.notes: Cures Within Reach's AI Validation RFP funds small investigator-initiated proof-of-concept, Phase I or Phase IIA trials that test an already-approved therapy in a new indication, where AI-generated evidence forms part of the preclinical rationale. It sits squarely at the intersection of the PI's first two angles: a computational or AI-derived repurposing hypothesis (angle 1) tested in a small IIT (angle 2), and the sponsor's "unsolved disease" definition explicitly covers settings where "many patients develop resistance to the therapy," which maps onto endocrine-resistant ER+ disease. The 2026 cycle is closed (LOI due 2026-06-26, now under review); the 2025 cycle had an August deadline, so the next release is projected for spring 2027 but no date is posted. The traps are financial and structural: the $100,000 budget is really $90,000 from CWR plus a required 10% institutional match, CWR money must be the sole, late or final funding for the stated aims (it cannot be seed money for a larger trial), indirects are capped at 30%, and the sponsor prefers rare diseases and off-patent drugs, so a common-cancer, on-patent proposal starts at a scoring disadvantage. Note also that CWR states it may reject applications substantially written by generative AI. The realistic play is a lean, drug-donated or add-on cohort (for example an off-patent repurposed agent layered onto standard endocrine therapy or an ADC backbone) whose only unmet funding is in the $100,000 range, with an AI workflow diagram prepared with a Rice or BCM data-science collaborator. record.eligibility: No eligibility criteria, application form, or deadline are published anywhere on the site. The awardee list (2006-2020) consists of Houston Texas Medical Center faculty at MD Anderson and Baylor College of Medicine, mostly MD or MD/PhD clinician-investigators, with no disease-area restriction (melanoma, GI, hepatobiliary, proteomics, ovarian biology). The PI, as a BCM MD assistant professor, matches the historical recipient profile, but selection appears to be board- or relationship-driven rather than by open competition.
record.notes: Cancer Fighters of Houston is an all-volunteer 501(c)(3) formed in 1980 that raises money through galas and lectures and periodically hands a "Seed Grant" of roughly $15,000-$25,000 to a Texas Medical Center investigator. The awardee page lists ten recipients between 2006 and 2020, including two at BCM (2014, 2015) and several at MD Anderson, with nothing posted for 2021-2026 even though the group still runs an annual fall fundraiser. There is no RFA, no application form, no deadline, and no eligibility text; awards appear to be chosen by the board through personal relationships. For the PI this is a possible source of modest pilot money for a ctDNA or registry feasibility project, not a mechanism to apply to. The trap is treating it as a deadline-bearing opportunity or spending effort drafting a proposal nobody has asked for. The sensible next step is a single inquiry to BCM Foundation Relations or the Duncan Cancer Center development office asking whether CFOH still makes seed grants and how recipients are chosen; if the answer is yes, a one-page concept could be held ready ahead of the October gala. Record as inactive-but-recurring philanthropy and revisit only if the awardee list updates.

record.eligibility: Open to investigators holding a PhD, MD, or equivalent at tax-exempt (501(c)3) research institutions in the United States. Applicants must either partner with an organization that delivers healthcare services or be based in a research unit embedded in a healthcare organization. The page states no career-stage restriction, no tenure-track requirement, and no prohibition on clinical duties. Projects must test approaches and tools that healthcare organizations can readily use to improve the value of the care they deliver; the program is not disease-specific.
record.notes: The Donaghue Foundation's Greater Value Portfolio is an annual national program that funds two-year projects (up to $500,000 plus 10% indirects) testing approaches and tools health systems can readily adopt to improve the value of care; cohorts have been funded every year from 2015 through 2025. The 2026 cycle (LOI April 30, full application August 20, start January 1, 2027) is marked closed on the page and no 2027 dates are posted, so the PI should expect an LOI in roughly April 2027. It fits the PI's real-world-data and equity angles rather than the ER+/HER2+ biology work: a credible pitch would be a pragmatic test of an EHR- or ctDNA-informed pathway (for example, de-escalating low-value surveillance or imaging in early breast cancer) deployed inside a delivery system such as Harris Health or Baylor St. Luke's, with cost and equity outcomes. The trap is submitting a disease-biology or biomarker-discovery proposal; the program rewards operational tools a health system can use tomorrow, and the applicant must show a formal healthcare-delivery partner or an embedded research unit. There is no stated career-stage cap, tenure gate, or clinical-duty restriction, and the MD-only requirement is met. The FAQ, announcement, and LOI guidance PDFs are hosted on Adobe share links that could not be read, so any per-institution limit or exclusion list remains unverified; the PI should download those documents when the 2027 announcement appears and confirm with the BCM office of sponsored programs whether the 10% indirect rate is acceptable.

record.typical_month: June

record.eligibility: At the grant start date applicants must hold a doctoral degree (PhD, MD, MD/PhD or equivalent) and an independent faculty position (professor, assistant professor, research assistant professor, instructor or equivalent) at an academic, medical or research institution anywhere in the world; there are no citizenship or geographic requirements and no years-since-appointment cap. Applicants must be AACR Active members in good standing by the submission deadline. Ineligible: candidates for a further doctoral degree, U.S. federal employees or for-profit industry employees, postdoctoral or clinical research fellows working under a mentor, and current or past recipients (or collaborators on an active award) of an AACR-Novocure TTFields Research Grant. Clinical duties are not restricted, but the proposal must incorporate Novocure's Inovitro and/or inovivo systems and examine Tumor Treating Fields as a cancer therapeutic.
record.notes: The AACR-Novocure Cancer Research Grant is a $350,000, three-year award for independent faculty investigators whose project examines Tumor Treating Fields (TTFields) as a cancer therapeutic; the 2026 program guidelines require that the experimental design incorporate Novocure's Inovitro and/or inovivo systems, which Novocure supplies under a materials transfer agreement. Eligibility is permissive for the PI's profile: an MD assistant professor at an academic medical center qualifies, there is no career-stage cap, no citizenship requirement, and clinical duties are not restricted. The 2026 cycle closed on June 4, 2026 with a December 1, 2026 start; the guidelines reference past recipients, so the mechanism recurs, but a 2027 cycle is not posted and the award does not appear on AACR's under-development list as of 2026-09-14. The trap is topical: nothing in the PI's four angles (real-world data, investigator-initiated trials, ER+/HER2+ biomarkers, health equity) touches TTFields, and the mandatory in vitro device work means this cannot be repurposed as a computational or registry project. It is only worth pursuing if the PI wants to build a bench collaboration around TTFields in breast cancer (for example combination with HER2-directed agents or ADCs, or brain metastases, an area where Novocure runs trials), likely with a lab partner who would run the Inovitro work. Otherwise leave it in the database as a low-priority, well-characterized mechanism and revisit around April 2027 when the next guidelines would be posted. If pursued, AACR Active membership must be current by the deadline and indirects are limited to 10%.

record.eligibility: Direct access is available only to individuals affiliated with and approved by a Cosmos participating organization; the request form is aimed at people at a health system or academic medical center. record.notes: Epic Cosmos is not a funding mechanism; it is a free, de-identified, multi-institution EHR research dataset (310 million patients, 22.6 billion encounters across 387 organizations) that Epic makes available to researchers affiliated with and approved by a participating health system or academic medical center. It matters to the PI because it directly serves the top research angle: real-world treatment-pattern, sequencing, and outcome analyses in ER+/HER2+ disease and endocrine resistance, and equity analyses using the social-drivers data Cosmos captures, which can generate preliminary data for ACS, PCORI, or NIH real-world-data applications. The trap is assuming BCM access exists: the Cosmos site does not list participating organizations publicly, and the finder's claim that a BCM informatics dean sits on the Governing Council is not supported by the current governance page, which names 15 members from other institutions. Access is also institutionally gated: the PI cannot apply to Epic directly but must be approved through BCM's own research informatics or Epic analytics office, must attest to intended use and disclose funding sources, and needs Epic training before line-level SQL/Python/R work, which stays inside the secure portal. Next step is a query to BCM research informatics or the Duncan Cancer Center informatics core to confirm BCM's Cosmos participation and the internal approval path; if BCM does not participate, a collaborator at a participating Houston system is the alternative route. Record this as a data resource rather than an award.

record.eligibility: Any researcher may submit a data request through the Vivli platform; the administrator check confirms that all required form fields are complete and that "a qualified statistician is part of the team." Requests then go to the data contributor for a feasibility check and, for most contributors, to an Independent Review Panel or Scientific Committee that judges the research proposal on its merits. All requestors must complete data access training and execute a non-negotiable Data Use Agreement, which is signed by the requestor's institution (or covered under an existing master agreement); team members at other institutions sign their own DUA. No degree, career-stage, tenure-track, or clinical-duty restriction is stated.
record.notes: Vivli is a data-sharing platform, not a funder: a request yields individual participant-level data from contributed industry trials in a hosted secure research environment, with no money attached. It matters to the PI because Daiichi Sankyo, AstraZeneca, Pfizer, Novartis and Lilly are listed members, which is the route to pooled or secondary analyses of the DESTINY-Breast series and HR+/HER2+ registrational trials for questions on HER2 heterogeneity, ADC sequencing and endocrine resistance, i.e. the computational and translational angles. Requests are rolling; the process is an administrator completeness check (which requires a qualified statistician on the team), a contributor feasibility review, and an independent review panel judging scientific merit, followed by training and a non-negotiable DUA executed by BCM. The trap is treating this as a funded award or assuming any specific trial is available: ClinicalTrials.gov entries naming Vivli do not guarantee the contributor will release the dataset, and contributor-specific policies (timing after publication, endpoints, regulatory approval status) were not verifiable from the platform pages. A second trap is cost: the Standard environment is free for 365 days but bills $12/day thereafter, so analysis plans should finish within a year or budget the overage. Next step: search the Vivli catalog for the target NCT numbers, confirm a biostatistician collaborator, and pair the request with a funded mechanism (e.g., a pilot or a Komen/BCRF-type secondary-analysis award) that can cover analyst effort.

record.award_text: Not a funding award. Access to banked, non-reserved biospecimens and annotated clinical/outcome data from completed phase 2/3 and phase 3 NCTN trials (Navigator inventory described as over 2 million to 3 million specimens). Investigators receive a feasibility assessment and cost estimate; after CCSC approval they must document their own funding for Group biospecimen processing/shipping fees, data collection/processing fees, and laboratory work within 12 months or specimens return to inventory.
record.indirects: n/a - no funds awarded; investigator pays Group processing, shipping and data fees from other sources
record.typical_month: any (rolling LOI; proposals accepted by CTEP PIO at least 6 weeks before a standing CCSC review date are scheduled for that call)
flags: not-funding: biospecimen and clinical-data access only
requires CTEP investigator registration for the proposal PI
funding documentation due within 12 months of approval or specimens return to inventory
rolling: proposals queued to standing CCSC review calls, roughly 6+ weeks lead
priority to validation of pre-specified biomarkers and predictive over prognostic markers
publication and NCI pre-submission review obligations
record.eligibility: Requests for NCTN biospecimens from completed NCTN trials may be submitted by investigators in the research community, not only members of the NCTN Groups. The proposal PI must be a CTEP-registered investigator in every submission format. Requests go through the NCTN Navigator (LOI for feasibility review, then a full CCSC Proposal Submission Form with letters of support including one from the study's primary statistician) or directly to the Group bank for trials not in Navigator; if any trial in a multi-trial request is in Navigator the whole request must go through Navigator. Approved projects must document funding within 12 months and publish all results, including negative ones.
record.notes: The NCTN Core Correlative Sciences Committee pathway is NCI's standing mechanism for obtaining banked specimens and outcome-annotated clinical data from completed phase 2/3 and phase 3 cooperative-group trials; it provides no money and instead delivers a feasibility assessment and cost estimate. For the PI it is the most direct route to trial-quality tissue and plasma from completed breast trials (Alliance, NRG, SWOG, ECOG-ACRIN) for HER2-heterogeneity, endocrine-resistance, ADC-response or ctDNA/MRD biomarker validation, and an approved CCSC project is a strong preliminary-access statement inside an R01, R21, DoD BCRP or K-level application. The trap is sequencing: CCSC approval releases nothing until funding is documented, and the 12-month clock starts at the approval letter, so the PI should either hold a funded award that can absorb Group processing, shipping and data fees, or time the LOI so a pending grant decision lands inside that window. The evaluation guidelines favor validation of locked prediction models and pre-specified predictive biomarkers with power calculations and false-discovery control, so exploratory discovery pitches score poorly. The PI must be CTEP-registered (routine for a clinical trialist at an NCTN member site) and must recruit the trial's primary statistician for a letter of support, which usually means engaging the relevant Group breast committee first. Next step is to browse the public catalog at nctnbanks.cancer.gov for candidate trials, then submit a Navigator LOI; proposals accepted at least six weeks before a standing review date are scheduled for that call, with decisions expected about two weeks after review.
record.evidence: nctnbanks.cancer.gov/about/policy.html: "Requests for NCTN Biospecimens from completed NCTN clinical trials may be submitted by investigators in the research community, not only members of the NCTN Groups." (open to non-members); "investigators will be provided with a feasibility assessment and cost estimate upon review of the request" (no funding provided); "based on a review and approval by the NCTN Core Correlative Sciences Committee (NCTN-CCSC)" (review body). dctd.cancer.gov/research/networks/nctn/ccsc: "Cancer Therapy Evaluation Program (CTEP)-registered investigators may submit proposals" for "Banked, non-reserved biospecimens from phase 2/3 or phase 3 NCTN clinical trials" (eligibility and scope). .../ccsc/review: "All submission formats require that the proposal PI be a CTEP-registered investigator."; "Proposals received and accepted by PIO ≥ 6 weeks before the standing CCSC review date will be scheduled for the call 6 weeks hence, pending review slot availability." (rolling cycle); decision "within 2 weeks of Committee proposal review". .../ccsc/approval: "Documentation of funding" covering "NCTN Network Group biospecimen processing and shipping fees" and "NCTN Network Group data collection and processing fees" must arrive "within 12 months of the date of the approval letter" (investigator pays; 12-month clock). .../ccsc/evaluation: "Priority is given to studies validating fully specified (locked) prediction models and/or validation of pre-specified biomarkers"; "Predictive biomarkers are preferred over prognostic biomarkers."

record.eligibility: Applicant must be currently in post-graduate training or have completed post-graduate training within the last 10 years, and be engaged in clinical, translational, imaging, or basic cancer research (or non-cancer research applicable to cancer). Applicant must be at, or working under a mentor at, an institution that is a member of any adult-cancer NCTN research group (Alliance, CCTG, ECOG-ACRIN, NRG Oncology, or SWOG). The abstract must present research not entirely duplicative of work already published or presented at a major meeting, limited to 2800 characters, submitted by email to the Mentoring Program Administrator on the downloadable Abstract Submission Form. No faculty-rank ceiling is stated beyond the 10-year post-training window.
record.notes: The ECOG-ACRIN Young Investigator Symposium is an annual mentoring event at the Fall Group Meeting, not a funding mechanism: up to eight early-career investigators present an abstract, ECOG-ACRIN pays travel and lodging, and two receive awards of distinction at the plenary. It matters to the PI mainly as a low-cost route into ECOG-ACRIN committee visibility ahead of a Breast Committee concept submission (see the held ecog-acrin-breast-concept record), and a symposium presentation of ctDNA/MRD real-world data or an ER+/HER2+ biomarker analysis would fit the clinical/translational categories. The PI qualifies on the 10-year post-training window and on institutional eligibility, since membership in any adult NCTN group counts, though BCM's current group membership should be confirmed. The trap is timing: the 2026 abstract deadline is 2026-09-17 at 11:59 PM Eastern, three days from the verification date, and the abstract must not be entirely duplicative of published or previously presented work. If a suitable unpresented dataset exists, the PI should download the Abstract Submission Form, keep the abstract under 2800 characters, and email it with optional supporting materials to the Mentoring Program Administrator; otherwise, plan for the September 2027 cycle. Meeting dates and location for the 2026 Fall Group Meeting are not posted on the program page.

record.eligibility: Nominee must hold an MD, MD/PhD or equivalent degree, currently possess a K08 or equivalent career development award, and be within 1-5 years of the first faculty appointment; the page states that timeframe is flexible for extenuating circumstances. Nominee must not yet hold an R01 or equivalent (a favorable score without a notice of award is acceptable; DP5 recipients are not excluded). Nomination must come from an ASCI member in good standing, who need not be at the nominee's institution and who initiates it through the member portal. No tenure-track or clinical-duty restriction is stated.
record.notes: The ASCI Young Physician-Scientist Award is a national honorific for early-faculty MDs on K-type awards, not a research grant: recipients get a $750 travel honorarium, Joint Meeting registration, a guaranteed JCI Insight first-round review and two years of programming. The 2027 cycle is open now with nominations accepted through 2026-10-09, submitted by an ASCI member through the member portal. For this PI the honor would carry weight on a promotion dossier and signal physician-scientist standing, but three gates stand in the way: the nominee must currently hold a K08 or equivalent, must not hold an R01-equivalent, and should be within 1-5 years of first faculty appointment. Several years past first appointment, the PI is outside the stated window, and the page's flexibility language is reserved for extenuating circumstances, so a nomination would need a documented case (for example, clinical-duty disruption or a late K start). The trap is treating this as a funding opportunity or as automatically open to any assistant professor; it is neither. Next step: confirm whether the PI holds an active K-series or equivalent award and no R01; if so, identify an ASCI member at BCM or a collaborating TMC institution willing to nominate before 2026-10-09 and frame the extenuating-circumstances case in the nomination. If no K award is in hand, drop this from the active list and treat it as a future-cycle honor only.

record.eligibility: Applicants must hold an MD, PhD, DO, PharmD or equivalent doctoral-level degree, be US citizens, nationals or permanent residents, and be employed by and conduct research supported by a domestic nonprofit or government entity. New applicants must have total qualifying educational debt equal to or exceeding 20 percent of institutional annual base salary and must contractually commit to an average of at least 20 hours per week of qualified research for an initial two years; NIH research funding is not required and there is no career-stage or years-since-appointment cap. Research must fall within a FOCUS area designated by the sponsoring Institute, and NCI's FOCUS areas are data science, computational biology, informatics, prevention, cancer control and population sciences, and human-based approaches to cancer biology, diagnosis and treatment. Ineligible are individuals receiving any research support or salary from a for-profit organization, federal employees working more than 20 hours per week, current IRTA/CRTA recipients, and anyone with a federal judgment lien; only one LRP application per fiscal year is permitted.
record.notes: The NIH Extramural Loan Repayment Program for Facilitating Opportunities in Cutting-edge Science (LRP-FOCUS, L70) repays up to $50,000 per year of qualified educational debt for doctoral-level investigators who commit to at least 20 hours per week of research in an Institute-designated emerging or high-priority area. The FY2027 notice NOT-OD-26-083 (released July 13, 2026, replacing the former LRP-REACH notice NOT-OD-25-094) confirms the cycle opened September 1, 2026 and closes November 19, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. EST, with repayment starting between July 1 and September 30, 2027. It matters to the PI because NCI's published FOCUS areas name data science, computational biology, informatics and cancer control and population sciences, which is a closer match to the PI's EHR, ctDNA/MRD and registry work than the generic clinical-research definition under LRP-CR, and there is no career-stage cap and no NIH-funding prerequisite. The award is personal debt relief, not research money, and is disease-agnostic, so breast or ER+/HER2+ relevance carries no weight in review. The trap is threefold: the PI must still carry educational debt of at least 20 percent of base salary, must be able to certify a 50 percent research effort quarterly while holding clinical duties, and may submit only one LRP application per fiscal year, so L70 and the held L30 (LRP-CR) are mutually exclusive rather than additive. A further trap is the exclusion of anyone receiving research support or salary from a for-profit organization, which must be reconciled against industry consulting and industry-sponsored trial arrangements. Next step: confirm remaining debt and protected time, then contact the NCI LRP scientific liaison to confirm that computational and real-world-evidence oncology fits NCI's FOCUS priorities and to decide between L30 and L70 before registering in ASSIST and submitting by November 19, 2026.

record.award_text: Direct costs up to $450,000 per year in the UG3 phase and up to $800,000 per year in the UH3 phase; total project period up to 5 years; approximately 6-8 UG3/UH3 awards anticipated (Grants.gov lists 8). Phase lengths are not fixed in the NOFO.

record.eligibility: Standard NIH organizational eligibility (higher-education institutions, nonprofits, for-profits, governments); foreign organizations and foreign components are allowed but foreign subawards are not. Any individual with the skills and resources to lead the work may serve as PD/PI; there is no career-stage, degree, or tenure requirement. The application must use the multiple-PI mechanism with at least one MPI from an academic institution and at least one MPI from a for-profit industrial partner with a track record or strong potential in development, regulatory approval, or commercialization of medical software; nonprofits do not satisfy the industrial-partner requirement. Institutions may submit more than one scientifically distinct application.
record.notes: RFA-RM-27-012 is the first-cycle Data-to-Model Academic-Industrial Partnership NOFO of the new NIH Common Fund PRIMED-AI program, a UG3/UH3 phased cooperative agreement (administered by NCI on behalf of NIH) to build AI-enabled, image-centered, multimodal clinical decision support tools headed toward Software as a Medical Device. Budgets run to $450,000 direct per year in UG3 and $800,000 direct per year in UH3 over up to five years, with roughly six to eight awards expected; applications are due 2026-10-19 with no letter of intent and no second receipt date. It matters to the PI because the disease-agnostic call explicitly names digital-twin CDS tools that fuse clinical imaging, genomic profiling, and real-world EHR and patient-reported data to model individual response trajectories, which is the PI's top computational and real-world-data angle; an HER2-heterogeneity or endocrine-resistance use case combining pathology or radiology images with ctDNA/MRD and EHR data is a credible framing, but breast cancer is not mentioned anywhere in the NOFO. The trap is the partnership rule: the application must be multi-PI with a designated MPI from a for-profit company that can credibly commercialize medical software, and foundations or research institutes do not count, so an academic-only imaging-AI team (BCM plus Rice, for example) is nonresponsive. A second trap is scope: projects that are not image-centered, that lack a defined intended use and user population, or that propose Phase III trials are listed as nonresponsive, and D2M-AIP is the pre-competitive model-building track while clinical-adoption studies belong under companion RFA-RM-27-013. With five weeks to the deadline and an industry MPI, leadership plan, IP terms, and milestone Gantt charts required, the PI should only pursue this cycle if an existing industry relationship and imaging-AI collaborator can be committed immediately; otherwise it is worth tracking for a possible reissue, since Common Fund programs typically run multiple rounds but this NOFO itself expires 2026-10-20. Next step: contact ODPRIMED-AI@od.nih.gov and the Common Fund program webinar materials, and confirm whether BCM or a Houston partner has a for-profit imaging-AI collaborator willing to serve as MPI.

The structural barrier for the PI is membership: eligibility requires being rostered at an Alliance member institution and belonging to an Alliance CCP committee, and Baylor College of Medicine is not on the Alliance member list (the Houston members are Houston Methodist Hospital and MD Anderson, both LAPS sites). The 2023 FAQ allowed a non-member-institution applicant to apply through an Alliance institution where they hold an appointment, with funds flowing to that institution, so the realistic path is an adjunct or affiliate appointment at Houston Methodist or MDACC plus CCP committee membership, arranged well before any reopened deadline. Topically the mechanism fits the PI's equity and real-world-data angles (health outcomes, minority and underserved populations, retrospective analyses of Alliance breast trial data such as biomarker or ctDNA correlates) far better than an ER+/HER2+ therapeutic question, and it will not fund an investigator-initiated treatment trial. The trap is treating the 2023 terms and November/December timing as current: the review may change the award size, tracks or eligibility. Next step: the PI should confirm whether any Alliance roster or committee standing exists through Houston collaborators, contact the CCP administrator (Jill Oliveri, DrPH, jill.oliveri@osumc.edu) to ask when the program will reopen, and re-verify the program page in late 2026.

record.eligibility: Standard NIH organizational eligibility: higher-education institutions, nonprofits, for-profits, governments, and foreign organizations may apply. Any individual with the skills, knowledge, and resources to carry out the work may serve as PD/PI; there is no degree, career-stage, or tenure requirement and no bar on clinical duties. Each partnership must include at least one academic and one industrial organization, with industry involved from the beginning of the project. The mechanism supports translation of technologies past proof of principle (enhance, adapt, optimize, validate); it does not fund basic research, commercial production, or phase III trials.
record.notes: PAR-25-337 is the current reissue (of PAR-21-206) of NCI's long-running Academic-Industrial Partnerships R01, which funds the translation of diagnostic and treatment technologies from demonstration of possibility to a status useful in a chosen clinical setting, with a $499,000 direct-cost annual cap over up to five years. It matters to the PI because NCI's stated interests include liquid-biopsy multiomic platforms, minimal residual disease monitoring, and machine-learning models, which line up with the PI's ctDNA/MRD and real-world-data angle; a validation study of a commercial MRD assay in ER+/HER2+ or endocrine-resistant breast cancer, run with the vendor as the industrial partner, is a natural shape for an application. The trap is treating the industrial partner as a subcontractor: reviewers score the partnership itself (complementary expertise, ability to work together), and the technology must already be past proof of principle, so a project built on a new academic assay or on basic mechanism will be judged nonresponsive. Applications that carry a trial are allowed only when translation is the primary motivation, and phase III trials are excluded; a purely observational or retrospective validation belongs under companion PAR-25-338 (Clinical Trial Not Allowed). Next receipt date is 2026-10-05, with further dates 2027-02-05, 2027-06-05, and 2027-10-05 before expiration on 2028-01-08. Recommended next step: identify a willing assay or data-platform company, confirm its investigators will hold substantive roles (MPI is permitted), and contact the NCI program staff listed on the NOFO to confirm that a breast-cancer MRD validation project fits the current portfolio before the February 2027 cycle.

It is real and open: grants.gov shows it posted 2026-05-19 with a closing date of 2027-03-01, standard NIH organizational eligibility, and no career-stage or track restrictions, so the PI is eligible to lead one. It matters to this profile because it pairs a national biospecimen resource with longitudinal EHR data, a natural substrate for the PI's real-world-data and biomarker angles (for example, plasma-based assays or risk models across a large, diverse cohort) without building a cohort. The trap is that the X01 carries no funds: the applicant must already have, or concurrently secure, an external sponsor (foundation, industry or a separate NIH award) to pay for assays and analysis, and must commit to depositing new data into the Researcher Workbench; the cohort is also general-population, so breast-specific and ER+/HER2+ questions will be underpowered unless framed as risk, early detection or germline questions. record.notes: The NIH Director's New Innovator Award (DP2) is the Common Fund's large early-career mechanism for exceptionally creative investigators, worth $475,000 per year for five years with no preliminary data required. The prior cycle (RFA-RM-27-002) closed August 17, 2026, and grants.gov posted the next-cycle forecast (RFA-RM-28-002) on September 3, 2026 with an estimated NOFO post date of March 15, 2027 and an estimated application due date of August 19, 2027. It matters to this profile because the PI may still hold ESI status provided the ten-year window since the end of clinical training has not lapsed and no R01-equivalent has been awarded, and the FAQ confirms the 25% floor applies to research effort rather than total effort, which suits a clinician with substantial patient-care duties. The trap is twofold: any prior substantial NIH award as PI or MPI ends eligibility outright, and a conventional biomarker or trial proposal will not compete; DP2 review rewards a bold, field-changing idea, so a computational or real-world-data project would need to be framed as a paradigm shift rather than an extension of existing work. The award is not track-gated (an independent research position suffices) and there is no institutional cap, but only one application per investigator per cycle is permitted. Next step: the PI should confirm ESI status in eRA Commons now, watch for the NOFO in spring 2027, and start shaping a single-PI concept well ahead of the August 2027 estimated deadline. record.eligibility: The LOI page states the program is open to academic and community-based physicians and researchers worldwide who wish to pursue independent scientific studies, although the process is framed as empowering members of the Caris Precision Oncology Alliance (POA). Inquiries are screened on data availability, testability of the hypothesis, and lack of overlap with already-approved projects, and all proposals are assessed by the Caris Scientific Review Committee. Baylor College of Medicine and the other Houston institutions do not appear on the POA member list (Texas members shown are UT Health San Antonio Mays and UT Southwestern Simmons), so the PI would submit under the worldwide-researcher route or through a collaborator at a member institution. Approved studies are expected to result in publication, and a fully executed contract is required before data access.
record.notes: The Caris Letter of Intent program is a no-cost, rolling route to investigator-initiated analyses of the Caris clinico-molecular database through the CODEai platform, with support from the Caris research team; it is a data resource, not a funding mechanism. It matters to the PI because the real-world molecular and outcomes data are directly usable for priority-1 real-world data questions and priority-3 questions on ER+/HER2+ disease, HER2 heterogeneity, and endocrine resistance, and an accepted project yields an ASCO-cycle abstract and publication with no budget required. The trap is timing: the September 1, 2026 inquiry cutoff for ASCO 2027 has already passed, and Caris states that inquiries submitted between September 2, 2026 and January 31, 2027 will not be reviewed until February 2027, so a submission now cannot target ASCO 2027. A second trap is institutional standing, since BCM is not on the POA member list; the worldwide-researcher route is stated on the page, but a collaborator at a POA member (nearest Texas members are UT Health San Antonio and UT Southwestern) may improve review odds and access to working groups. The PI should draft a focused, hypothesis-driven inquiry with a clearly testable question that does not overlap approved POA projects, submit it in early 2027 for review in February 2027, and start BCM contract review early because a fully executed agreement is required before any data access. The PI should also check whether BCM's cancer center has any existing Caris institutional agreement that would simplify contracting. record.eligibility: Only NCTN Groups and NCORP Research Bases can apply, and they submit through the CTEP or DCP Protocol Information Office. The study must belong to an NCI trial concept or protocol. Eligible trials are randomized phase 2/3 treatment trials, randomized phase 2/3 prevention trials, randomized symptom-science/supportive-care trials, and non-randomized phase 2/3 treatment trials (integral studies only). An individual investigator takes part by leading the correlative study inside a group concept, not by applying alone.
record.notes: BIQSFP is NCI CCCT's program for paying for biomarker, imaging and symptom-science/QOL studies that sit inside NCTN and NCORP trials. It is the standard way to fund a ctDNA/MRD, HER2-heterogeneity or endocrine-resistance correlative inside an SWOG, NRG, Alliance or ECOG-ACRIN breast trial, so it fits the PI's biomarker and trial angles. The trap is that no individual can apply. The group or NCORP Research Base submits through the CTEP/DCP Protocol Information Office, and an integral study must go in at the same time as the parent concept. The PI should therefore write the correlative aims and a BIQSFP budget into any concept sent through the held committee routes (swog-breast-committee-concept, nrg-oncology-concept-submission, alliance-breast-committee-concept, ecog-acrin-breast-concept) rather than treat this as a separate grant. A real-time integrated study can follow within about three months of concept approval. Non-real-time studies are accepted only in response to a CCCT call, so it is worth watching for one. Next steps: confirm that BCM is an NCTN member through the relevant group and ask that group's breast committee and statistics centre about BIQSFP planning.

record.notes: The Count Me In Metastatic Breast Cancer Project (CMI-MBC) is a patient-partnered cohort whose tumor exome and RNA-seq data are distributed through the NCI Genomic Data Commons, with controlled files under dbGaP phs001709 and more data on cBioPortal. It provides no money. It is still valuable to the PI because it is a free, breast-specific metastatic cohort that links genomics to clinical histories, which fits the computational and real-world-data angle and could support endocrine-resistance or HER2-alteration questions as preliminary data for a funded application. The main trap is treating it as representative real-world data: participants self-enrolled and much of the clinical detail is patient-reported, so it works better for hypothesis generation or validation than for effect estimates. The size of the HER2-positive and triple-positive subset is not stated on the GDC page and may be small. Next step: explore the open cBioPortal study to check subtype counts and clinical fields, then file a dbGaP request for phs001709 only if exome or RNA-level reanalysis is needed.

record.notes: The ASCO Data Library is a fee-based route to ASCO-held datasets for research, and it awards no money. ASCO's Center for Research and Analytics (CENTRA) runs the reviews, and requests are taken at any time. The datasets are the TAPUR Study (a phase II basket trial of targeted drugs, with clinical and genomic data), the ASCO COVID-19 Registry and 40 years of meeting abstracts. It fits the PI's first angle (computational and real-world data) as a source for secondary analysis. It could also serve the HER2/ADC angle if TAPUR's HER2-targeted cohorts include enough breast patients. The trap is to treat it as funding: it costs money and should be budgeted inside another grant. The library page does not name the HER2- or CDK-pathway cohorts, so the Dataset Description and Data Dictionary PDFs should be checked before assuming breast-relevant arms exist. A breast-specific question may also be underpowered in a pan-tumor basket trial. The next step is to read the TAPUR Dataset Description, email CENTRA for a fee estimate, and only then submit a Research Project Proposal Application alongside a funded computational project.

record.eligibility: Applicants must be researchers at a public or private institution of higher education or at a 501(c)(3) nonprofit. They need a doctorate or master's degree in health services research, social sciences, epidemiology, medicine, law or a related field, plus evidence of having designed and conducted health disparities or health equity research. Projects must study disparities among Medicare, Medicaid or CHIP enrollees in underserved populations, such as racial and ethnic minorities, people with disabilities, LGBTQ+ people, rural residents or people with limited English proficiency.
record.notes: HEDAP is run by the CMS Office of Minority Health. It gives selected researchers a funded seat in the CMS VRDC for up to 36 months to study health disparities using restricted Medicare, Medicaid and CHIP data. It fits the PI's real-world-data and equity angles: for example, disparities in breast cancer treatment patterns, CDK4/6 inhibitor or ADC uptake, or endocrine therapy adherence among Medicare enrollees. A VRDC seat normally costs a lot, so the award has real value, but it is in-kind data access with no salary or project funds. The trap is status. The current opportunity, CMS-2L2-25-001, is a FY2025 forecast first posted in July 2024. It was last touched on Grants.gov on 2026-05-13 and still has no estimated post date or due date, so a NOFO may never appear. Eligibility also requires a demonstrated record of disparities or equity research, so the PI would need prior equity publications or a co-investigator who has them. Next steps: subscribe to Grants.gov notifications for CMS-2L2-25-001, email HEResearch@cms.hhs.gov to ask whether a FY2026 or FY2027 NOFO is planned, and check whether BCM or a Texas Medical Center partner already holds VRDC access that could replace this route.
record.evidence: CMS primary page, fetched 2026-09-23: "a 'seat' in the CMS Virtual Research Data Center (VRDC) for a period of up to 36 months". It also says "A notice of funding opportunity (NOFO) will be announced for researchers to apply", which establishes that no application window is open. Degree requirement from the same page: "doctorate or master's degree in health services research, social sciences, epidemiology, medicine, law or other related scientific/medical fields". record.eligibility: Institutional eligibility is broad: public and private institutions of higher education, nonprofits, for-profits, small businesses, state/local governments, tribal organizations, and non-domestic (foreign) institutions are listed. No individual career-stage restriction is stated in the forecast. Awards are multidisciplinary Centers to advance the science of AI science, so the PI would realistically participate as a clinical-domain investigator or pilot-project lead inside a BCM, Rice or TMC center application rather than as contact PI.
record.notes: Bridge2AI Stage 2 is a forecasted NIH Common Fund U24 cooperative agreement (RFA-RM-28-010). It would fund 3-5 multidisciplinary Centers that build a network for the "science of AI science": evaluating AI models built on Stage 1 AI-ready datasets, setting reproducibility and trustworthiness frameworks, running expert panels, cross-training, and supporting pilot research. The only link to the PI's profile is the computational and real-world-data angle. Nothing in the forecast is about oncology, and the centers are about AI methodology rather than disease questions, so a breast-cancer EHR or ctDNA use case would only enter as a demonstration or pilot project. The trap is treating it as an individual grant: realistically the PI would be a clinical-domain co-investigator or pilot lead on a Rice or BCM data-science center application, and the dates are estimates only. As next steps, the PI could ask Rice or BCM computational groups whether anyone is building a center team, attend the Bridge2AI All Hands and Open House if it fits, and check whether the NOFO, expected around January 2027, sets a limited-submission cap per institution.

record.career_cap: Mentored award for investigators not yet independent. The notice states no specific time-since-degree limit; the IC-specific rules (for example NCI's) are not yet published.
record.eligibility: Intended for clinician research scientists who hold clinical doctoral degrees and are working toward research independence under an experienced mentor. KC1 consolidates the K08, K23 and K38 activity codes and takes effect for due dates on or after October 12, 2027. K award funds may not support conducting a clinical trial, a feasibility study or an ancillary study. Awardees may take part in trials their mentors lead but need separate funding to lead their own. Neither the notice nor the forecast states career-stage, time-since-degree, effort or citizenship criteria; the NOFO (estimated posting 2027-07-13) will define them.
record.notes: KC1 is the NIH's new consolidated mentored clinician-scientist K award. It replaces K08, K23 and K38 for applications due on or after October 12, 2027, and the Grants.gov forecast PA-28-047 estimates the NOFO will post on July 13, 2027. It matters to this profile because the held K08 and K23 records (PA-24-182/181, PA-24-185/184) expire by July 13, 2027, so those parent announcements have only a few cycles left. The main trap is the new rule that K funds cannot support conducting a clinical trial. After the switch, a K award cannot fund an investigator-initiated trial the PI leads, so the IIT angle needs a separate R-series, foundation or industry funding line. A second risk is the PI's seniority: the PI would need to confirm fit for a mentored award at their career stage, and NCI-specific K eligibility rules for KC1 are not yet published. The likely 75% research-effort requirement also has to be squared with the PI's clinical duties. If a K is a realistic goal, the PI should weigh applying under the current K08/K23 parents in the remaining 2026-2027 cycles and confirm NCI candidacy with BCM OSP and the NCI program officer. The PI should re-check PA-28-047 when it posts in July 2027.
record.evidence: NOT-OD-26-098 (released August 12, 2026) establishes KC1, 'Mentored Clinician Research Scientist Career Development Awards', consolidating K08, K23 and K38. Implementation is 'beginning with due dates on or after October 12, 2027', and any active NOFO using current K codes 'will be expired by July 13, 2027' (K00, K12, K43 and K76 are unaffected). The notice also says 'K award funds may not be used to support the conduct of a clinical trial, clinical trial feasibility study, or ancillary study'.
